title: Egg omelet or scrambled egg with cheese and meat

content.title: About
content.content: An egg omelet or scrambled egg with cheese and meat is a dish made from eggs, dairy, and meat ingredients. Eggs provide high‑quality protein and nutrients, cheese adds calcium and flavor, and meat contributes extra protein and a savory taste.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Eggs are one of the most affordable sources of complete protein.
Cheese boosts the calcium and vitamin D content of the dish.
Meat (such as ham or bacon) adds rich flavor and iron.
Traditionally, omelets are cooked over medium heat to keep a soft texture.
The dish is popular worldwide, from American breakfasts to European appetizers.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Eggs and meat together provide high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Calcium and vitamin D
items.content: Cheese contributes calcium for bone health, while vitamin D aids its absorption.

items.title: Iron and vitamin B12
items.content: Meat supplies iron and vitamin B12, important for blood formation and nervous system function.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: The dish contains virtually no carbs, making it suitable for low‑carb diets.

items.title: Satiety
items.content: The combination of protein and fat promotes long‑lasting fullness.

items.title: High saturated fat content
items.content: Cheese and meat can be high in saturated fats, so portion control is advised, especially for heart‑related conditions.

items.title: Allergy to eggs or dairy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to eggs or cheese.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Eggs contain cholesterol; people with elevated cholesterol levels should consume them in moderation.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: Processed meat additions are often salty, increasing sodium intake.

content.title: How to Cook
content.content: Beat the eggs, stir in grated cheese and finely chopped meat. Heat a small amount of oil in a skillet, pour in the mixture, and cook over medium heat, stirring gently until the eggs set but remain tender. Optionally add herbs, spices, or vegetables for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Best enjoyed fresh. If needed, store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours. Reheat in a skillet or microwave, adding a little oil to prevent drying out.
